fact: Fort Collins' Land Use Code lets the Director make an exception to its development turf ban only for artificial turf on an athletic field of play, and only where the use is appropriate, adds no pollutants that could cause environmental impairment and has no reasonable alternative.
quote: The Director may approve an exception to allow artificial turf to be installed on an athletic field of play if the installation is not prohibited under C.R.S. 37-99-103 and if the Director determines the use is appropriate, the use does not add pollutants that could cause environmental impairment, and alternatives are not reasonable. Any exception to allow artificial turf must be noted in the landscape plan.
source_label: Fort Collins Land Use Code 5.10.1, Artificial Turf and Plants (Ordinance No. 008, 2025; same text in the current Article 5)
notes: Read in Ord. 008, 2025 (pdftotext) and again in the current LUC Article 5 PDF on fortcollins.gov (read in a browser; curl gets 403), where the clause now sits under 5.10.1(F)(2)(d). The exception names only an athletic field of play: playgrounds, picnic grounds and putting greens, which HB25-1113 counts as functional turf, are not named. LUC phase 2 (commercial corridors) is in progress: re-read before recheck.

fact: In the developments its landscape standards cover, Fort Collins requires more than 50% living-plant cover in each landscape area and allows high-water turf grass, such as Kentucky bluegrass, only where people play or gather, such as playgrounds, sports fields, picnic grounds, parts of parks and golf playing areas, never in parking lots or medians.
quote: Not counting trees, more than 50% of a landscape area must be covered with living plants at maturity. The Director may approve an exception to this requirement if a determination is made that an area is too small for living landscape material and for irrigation to be reasonably feasible. … Irrigated turf grass with a high water requirement may only be planted according to planned use, only in areas or spaces used for recreation or for civic or community purposes. Such purposes may include playgrounds, sports fields or other athletics programming, picnic grounds, amphitheaters, portions of parks, and playing areas of golf courses. Such purposes do not include, and irrigated turfgrass with a high water requirement must not be planted in, parking lots or medians. … Irrigated turf grass with a high water requirement refers to high- or moderate-hydrozone sod forming grasses including species such as Poa pratensis (Kentucky bluegrass), and turf-type tall fescue (Festuca arundinacea) and their varieties and cultivars.
source_label: Fort Collins Land Use Code 5.10.1, Landscape Area Treatment: coverage and irrigated turf grass (Ordinance No. 008, 2025; same text in the current Article 5)
notes: Applies only where 5.10.1 applies (development landscape plans; existing single- and two-unit lots are exempt, see fc-luc-5.10.1). The live-grass list is the same list HB25-1113 uses to define functional artificial turf, which is the Fort Collins contrast: live bluegrass may go where artificial turf may not.

fact: Fort Collins' Streetscape Standards, adopted in December 2025, bar artificial turf and artificial plants from every streetscape, including parkways and medians, for private development and renovation applications submitted on or after January 1, 2026 and City capital projects installed from that date.
quote: These streetscape standards involve parameters for tree-lined streets and sidewalks, parkways, other landscaping along street edges, and landscaped medians in streets. … These standards apply to all projects involving streetscapes in the City right-of-way including: Private development projects for which an application is submitted on or after January 1, 2026. … City capital projects installed on and after January 1, 2026. … Any other renovation projects and efforts for which an application is submitted on or after January 1, 2026. … 4.2.2 Prohibitions. No artificial turf or artificial plants may be included in any streetscape.
source_label: City of Fort Collins Streetscape Standards (LCUASS Appendix C), Exhibit A to Ordinance No. 202, 2025, adopted on second reading Dec. 16, 2025
notes: Adoption confirmed in the Dec. 16, 2025 minutes (Jan. 6, 2026 council packet, consent item 7: 'Adopted on Second Reading'; first reading Dec. 2, 2025, unanimous): https://mccmeetings.blob.core.usgovcloudapi.net/fortcollco-pubu/MEET-Packet-14d9c93a88a54e4fb54bdc665f57ee02.pdf. Staff called it Phase 1 of the update, aimed at SB24-005 compliance; Phase 2 runs through 2026-2027, so re-read before recheck. This supersedes the parkway wording in the UNVERIFIED shared record fc-parkway-live-plants; the current XIP residential packet (read in a browser 2026-09-25) also says of parkways: 'No bare dirt or artificial plants or turf.'

fact: On Fort Collins collector and local streets, a parkway takes either turf-type grass or mulched planting beds, which the abutting owner may choose regardless of HOA covenants where no development plan sets it and must install and maintain; non-turf plantings must reach 50% live cover within 3 years with no fences; and where an approved landscape plan sets the parkway, changing it takes a Parkway Landscaping Amendment.
quote: Two main approaches to landscaping parkways are allowed in collector and local streets: turf-type grasses, and mulched planting beds. … In areas where there is no development plan that specifies parkway landscaping, the owner of the property abutting the parkway may select either approach, regardless of any homeowners association (HOA) covenants that may apply to the development, and shall be responsible for the installation and maintenance of the parkway … 6.1.2 Approved development plans govern. In developments with approved landscape plans, the parkway landscaping must be in accordance with the plan. A HOA, or a property owner with notice to and opportunity for comment from the HOA, may request a Parkway Landscaping Amendment to an approved plan for parkway landscaping. … 6.1.7 Requirements for non-turf ground cover plantings: A. Landscaping must be designed, installed and maintained so that at least 50% of the area is covered with live plant material within 3 years from installation. … D. No fences or thorny/prickly plant material are allowed.
source_label: City of Fort Collins Streetscape Standards 6.1.1, 6.1.2 and 6.1.7, Exhibit A to Ordinance No. 202, 2025, adopted on second reading Dec. 16, 2025
notes: The no-fee point is its own record (fort-collins-co.parkway-amendment-no-fee). The 'no fences' clause sits under 6.1.7, the requirements for non-turf ground cover plantings.

fact: Fort Collins requires pet owners to remove waste from their own yard often enough to prevent a public nuisance, and its code counts animal odors that materially interfere with a neighbor at home as a public nuisance.
quote: The owner or keeper of any animal shall also be responsible for the periodic removal of feces deposited by such animal on property owned or exclusively occupied by such owner or keeper so as to prevent the creation of a public nuisance within the meaning of § 4-95. … For the purposes of this Section, a public nuisance includes an animal that is not a dangerous or vicious animal but is otherwise a safety or health hazard, damages or destroys the property of another or creates offensive odors which materially interfere with or disrupt another person in the conduct of lawful activities at such person's home.
source_label: Fort Collins City Code Secs. 4-71 (Removal of animal waste required) and 4-95 (Public nuisance prohibited)
notes: Read through the Municode API (CodesContent, productId 18005, jobId 498160), which returns all of Chapter 4. Sec. 4-95 node: CH4ANIN_ARTIIAN_DIV5COAN_S4-95PUNUPR. NOCO Humane (Larimer Humane Society) enforces animal control for the city.

fact: Fort Collins sets no fixed number of pets per home, only as many as can be kept healthy without a hazard or a nuisance to neighbors, and requires a license within 14 days of getting a dog or cat.
quote: In no event shall any person keep at his or her premises more pet animals than can be properly maintained in a healthy condition without presenting a health or safety hazard to the owners, keeper or others and without constituting a nuisance to the occupants of neighboring properties. … The owner or keeper of any dog or cat kept within the City shall secure from the City or the Humane Society, within fourteen (14) days of acquiring possession of said dog or cat, a license for the keeping of the same
source_label: Fort Collins City Code Secs. 4-116 (Quantity of pet animals restricted) and 4-31 (License required)
notes: Read through the Municode API (Chapter 4). Sec. 4-31(a) defenses: owner not yet in the City 30 days, or the animal is 4 months old or less. Online summaries claiming a Fort Collins cap of 4 adult dogs were not found in the City Code; the Code sets no number.

fact: Fort Collins requires pets other than birds to be kept under restraint except in designated areas such as dog parks, and any fence meant to enclose an animal must be securely constructed, adequate for the purpose and kept in good repair.
quote: At large shall mean outside of a fence or other enclosure which restrains the animal to a particular premises, whether on public or private property, and not under the control, by leash or lead, of the owner or keeper. … All pet animals, except birds, shall be kept under restraint. … The following shall be exempt from this prohibition: … (4) Animals in areas designated or signed permitting animals to be at large, such as dog parks. … (e) Fences which are intended as enclosures for any animal shall be securely constructed, adequate for the purpose and kept in good repair.
source_label: Fort Collins City Code Secs. 4-1 (definition of at large) and 4-93, Animals at large prohibited
notes: Read through the Municode API (Chapter 4, productId 18005, jobId 498160).

fact: Fort Collins needs no permit for a fence 6 feet tall or shorter, holds front-yard fences to 4 feet and rear-yard fences to 6 feet, keeps fences at least 2 feet from a public sidewalk and out of drainage easements, and prohibits electric fences in every zoning district.
quote: No permit required for fences 6 feet tall or shorter. Permit required for fences taller than 6 feet. … Front yard: Fences must be no taller than 4 feet. … Rear yard: Fences must be no taller than 6 feet. … Proximity to property lines: Fences must be on private property and no closer than 2 feet to a public sidewalk. … Fences and walls are prohibited within access and drainage easements. Electric fences are prohibited in all zoning districts. … In newer housing developments, restrictions regarding the size, type, style or location of a fence may exist through subdivision covenants or other private agreements.
source_label: City of Fort Collins, Rules for Common Projects: Fences (summarizing Land Use Code 4.3.5(C))
notes: fortcollins.gov returns 403 to curl; read in a headless browser 2026-09-25 (accordion text). Side-yard fences: 4 feet if in the front yard, 6 feet if in the rear yard; 42 inches in a visual clearance triangle. The page points to LUC 4.3.5(C) for the full rule; the LUC text itself was not read for this record.

fact: Fort Collins allows state-licensed day care homes as an accessory use of a house, and requires a child care center to have an outdoor play area of at least 1,200 square feet or 75 square feet per child for 33% of its capacity, fenced at least 6 feet high within or next to a residential district.
quote: Day care homes shall be permitted as an accessory use as defined in Article 7 provided that such homes are licensed by the State of Colorado … (G) Child Care Center (1) Outdoor Play Area is required to be the greater of either 1,200 sq. ft. or 75 sq. ft. per child of 33% of the child capacity of the center. (2) An outdoor play area as stated above shall not be required for drop-in child care centers. … Any such play area on the site of the child care center within or abutting any residential district shall be enclosed by a decorative solid wood fence, masonry wall or chain link fence with vegetation screening, densely planted. The height of such fence shall be a minimum of six (6) feet
source_label: Fort Collins Land Use Code 4.3.1(C)(2) Day Care Homes and 4.3.3(G) Child Care Center, Article 4 Use Standards
notes: The PDF returns 403 to curl; fetched in a headless browser and read with pdftotext 2026-09-25 (spacing artifacts in the extracted text removed). An outdoor play area is not required for drop-in child care centers (4.3.3(G)(2)). Article 7 defines a day care home as a state-licensed family child care home, infant/toddler home or experienced family child care provider home.

fact: Fort Collins Utilities pays commercial water customers, HOAs, schools and parks among them, $1.50 per square foot up to $15,000 per project for replacing grass with an eligible low-water landscape, and a site inside city limits needs a Minor Amendment before its site plan changes.
quote: All approved projects will receive a bonus incentive of $0.30 per square foot, up to $3,000, that is paid upfront. … Commercial water customers can receive $1.50 per square foot of area converted, up to $15,000 per project, for replacing grass with an eligible low-water landscape. … Eligible participants include: HOAs, Multi-unit residential complexes, Businesses, Faith-based organizations, Schools, Parks, Government entities … If your property falls within City limits, any change that results in a modification to the site plan on file with the City will require a Minor Amendment prior to any work being completed.
source_label: Fort Collins Utilities, Xeriscape Incentive Program page, XIP Commercial tab
notes: fortcollins.gov returns 403 to curl; read in a headless browser 2026-09-25. The eligible-participants line is a bulleted list on the page; the commas are ours. The page does not name artificial turf as an eligible landscape. Parkway-only changes use the free Parkway Amendment Application instead of a Minor Amendment.
